blocks.html:
Two weeks ago the call went beautifully. The prospect finished your sentences, called the problem “exactly it,” and said he was “really excited about this.” You moved the record to Yearning. You told your Managing Principal it was coming this quarter.

Then nothing. Two emails unanswered, one voicemail. When you finally reach him he says, “I still need to talk to my partner about it.” He was never at Yearning. He was at Bothered, with good manners.

Nobody lied. You moved the record on enthusiasm instead of evidence — and that one honest mistake moved your forecast, your principal’s planning and a client’s expectation. This lesson is about the difference between a good feeling and a stage you can defend.

blocks.prompt: Think of a deal you were sure about that stalled or died. What made you sure at the time — and what had the prospect actually said? (Optional — skip if you’d rather get started.)
blocks.coachContext: Opening reflection for a lesson on the B.U.Y.E.R.S. stage framework. The aim is for the learner to notice that their confidence usually came from tone and rapport, not from the prospect’s explicit words. Respond briefly and warmly; connect what they say to why each stage needs a quotable condition.

blocks.html:
By the end of this lesson you’ll be able to:

  1. Decide the true stage of a record from the prospect’s own words, using the B.U.Y.E.R.S. framework.
  2. Move a record the way OneAccord moves records — through Blueprint transitions — and correct one you moved wrongly.
  3. Gather the evidence that justifies a stage, including recording calls in Microsoft Teams with the prospect’s consent.

About 20 minutes. Keep Zoho open in a second tab.

One habit: before you click a stage, find the sentence that earns it. If you can’t quote it, you’re not there yet.

What a Buyer’s Journey record is

A Buyer’s Journey record is a potential piece of business — what other systems call an opportunity or a deal. It is always linked to a Contact (the person) and a Company, and it carries a value and an estimated close date. Those two numbers are only as trustworthy as the stage they sit at.

blocks.label: Find it now
blocks.instructions: Open the Buyer’s Journey module from your left menu and open any existing record. Look at the top of the record for the coloured transition buttons, and notice that the Stage field is locked.
blocks.confirmText: I’ve opened a Buyer’s Journey record and found its Blueprint buttons — continue

blocks.html:
The B.U.Y.E.R.S. framework

Every stage is named for what the prospect has to do — not what you believe or hope is true. Each stage has two conditions, and both must be met before you move forward.

StageWhat must be true — in the prospect’s own words
BotheredThe prospect can name the problem and articulate a real sense of urgency.
UnderstandThe prospect can describe the scope of the problem and the outcome they want, and asks how to get there.
YearningThe prospect explicitly states the desire — “this is what I need” — and can describe the approach in their own words.
ExplainableThe prospect can explain the value themselves and defend the decision to their own stakeholders.
ReadyThe prospect gives a specific verbal commitment — “I’m in” — and confirms final approval.
StartedThe contract is signed, payment is submitted and resources are committed.
FinishedThe engagement has actually been delivered. This is the real finish line, not the signature.

Eight rules hold it together: don’t skip steps. No urgency means no opportunity. To yearn, they must first understand. Yearning must be spoken and mutual. Buyers must be able to justify the decision to their own people. Enthusiasm is not commitment. If it isn’t paid for, it isn’t a deal yet. And celebrate the chance to deliver value, not the chance to book revenue.

How you move a record. Not by dragging and dropping: click the Blueprint transition button. It is a guided path, one honest step at a time, and the locked Stage field exists so nobody skips ahead.

Prove it — and ask first

Because every stage depends on the prospect’s words, OneAccord asks for evidence, not impressions.

  • Record your calls in Microsoft Teams. The transcript stays there, so you can go back and pull the actual sentence instead of your paraphrase of it.
  • Recording needs consent. Tell the prospect at the start of the call that you record for note-taking, and get their agreement before you begin. If they decline, don’t record — take careful notes and quote them directly.
  • The automated call-notes email. Once it is live, it will arrive after a call with notes and a suggested stage, worded so you can copy the language straight into Zoho. It is a documentation shortcut: you still click the Blueprint button yourself.

Moved it wrongly? Look for the transition labelled Correction – [stage], for example “Correction – Bothered.” Nobody expects perfection; they expect an honest record.

And when a record goes quiet? The Last Update timestamp is your cue to go and get the next real signal from the prospect — not to click the button and hope.

blocks.label: Set up your evidence trail
blocks.instructions: Open your Teams calling settings and confirm recording is available to you. Then write, in your own words, the one sentence you’ll use to ask a prospect’s permission to record — short, plain, and easy to say at the start of a call.
blocks.confirmText: I’ve checked my Teams recording and drafted my consent sentence — continue

blocks.prompt: According to B.U.Y.E.R.S., what must happen before you move a record from Understand to Yearning?
options: Thirty days must pass in the current stage.
The prospect explicitly states their desire in their own words and can describe the approach themselves.
The rep decides the prospect seems interested enough.
A Managing Principal signs off on the move.
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Correct — the prospect has to say it: “this is what I need,” plus the approach in their own words. Their words move the stage, not your read of the room.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Not quite. The prospect must explicitly state their desire in their own words and describe the approach themselves. Time in stage and your own confidence don’t count as conditions.

blocks.prompt: True or False: if a prospect seems excited and enthusiastic about your proposal, that is enough to move the record to Ready.
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right — enthusiasm is not commitment. Ready needs a specific verbal commitment (“I’m in”) plus confirmed final approval.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: False. Enthusiasm is not commitment. Ready requires a specific verbal commitment plus confirmed final approval, not good energy on the call.

blocks.promptHtml:
You record a discovery call with Marcus Bell, operations lead at a 40-person manufacturer. With his consent, the Teams transcript gives you these lines:

  • “Quoting is the bottleneck. Three people touch every quote and we still lose two days.”
  • “It’s costing us deals. Two this quarter went to a competitor who answered faster.”
  • “I don’t know what the fix looks like. What would you do?”
  • “Before we go further — my CFO has to be comfortable. She’s the one who killed the last system.”

Decide the stage you would set, quote the line or lines that earn it, name the condition that is missing, and say what your next conversation has to achieve.
rubric: Sets the stage at Understand (or Bothered moving to Understand) and justifies it with the urgency and scope lines
Explicitly identifies that Yearning is not yet earned because Marcus has not stated the desire or described the approach in his own words
Names the missing condition — the CFO’s buy-in — and treats it as a stakeholder to be won, not an obstacle
Sets a next step that gets Marcus to state the outcome and approach himself, rather than sending a proposal to create momentum
Does not overstate the record or the forecast
blocks.coachContext: Skill taught: set the Buyer’s Journey stage only on evidence in the prospect’s own words. B.U.Y.E.R.S.: Bothered (problem + real urgency), Understand (scope + desired outcome + asks how), Yearning (explicit desire + approach in own words), Explainable (can defend to stakeholders), Ready (verbal commitment + final approval), Started (signed, paid, resourced), Finished (delivered). Rules: don’t skip steps; no urgency = no opportunity; enthusiasm ≠ commitment; buyers must be able to justify it. The model answer: he is Understand — problem and urgency stated, asks how; desire and approach not yet in his words, and the CFO is an unmet Explainable condition. Good next step: a conversation that names the outcome he wants and asks him to describe the approach, plus early engagement with the CFO.

blocks.promptHtml:
Three weeks later Marcus says: “I want to do this. I’m sold. Let’s get started — send me something and I’ll get it approved.”

Then he adds: “I haven’t actually spoken to my CFO yet. But honestly, she’ll be fine — she trusts me.”

Decide the stage. Say what you would and would not do next, and quote the words that justify your decision.
rubric: Recognises Yearning (explicit desire) but does not advance to Ready
Names the unmet condition: no owner-level approval, and the buyer cannot yet defend the decision to the CFO
Plans a step that helps Marcus build his own case to the CFO — a business case, a joint conversation, or explicit discovery of her concerns
Resists sending a proposal purely to manufacture commitment
Records the conversation and the exact words, with consent, so the stage is defensible
blocks.coachContext: Skill taught: distinguish Yearning from Ready, and treat Explainable as a real gate. Model answer: Yearning is earned by the desire statement, but Ready needs a verbal commitment plus confirmed final approval — the CFO is unknown to the deal, so the buyer cannot yet defend it. The useful next step is to equip Marcus for the CFO conversation (or ask for it directly), not to send a proposal and wait. Note the pattern: a champion’s confidence about an unseen approver is a common source of slipped forecasts.

blocks.label: Apply it to your own pipeline
blocks.instructions:
Open your oldest open Buyer’s Journey record. Write down the exact sentence the prospect said that justifies its current stage.
  • If you can quote it, add it to the record’s notes so the next person can see the evidence.
  • If you cannot quote it, the stage is a guess. Use the Correction button to move it back to the stage you can defend, and note what you need to hear next.
Move at least one record today, in whichever direction the evidence points.
blocks.confirmText: I’ve checked one of my records against the evidence — continue
